source_metadata.exact_title: Clostridioides difficile-induced diarrhoea following dasatinib therapy

workflow.batching: single semantic pass; 3-page source did not require large-source batching

source_consistency_findings: The source strongly documents CDI in the reported patient but does not establish dasatinib causality; the dasatinib-CDI link is retained only as an author conclusion/hypothesis.
Dasatinib was restarted after a 1-month interruption and no diarrhoea recurred over 2 years, which weakens a simple reproducible drug-causality interpretation.
The discussion contains secondary literature estimates and mechanisms; these were not reclassified as primary-study results from this case report.

extraction_limitations: This is a single case report with no comparator, denominator beyond one patient, formal causality assessment, or controlled challenge/dechallenge design.
The article reports positive stool toxin A/B immunoassays but does not provide a broader microbiologic testing algorithm or strain data.
Background and discussion claims attributed to cited literature were not atomized as if they were generated by this case report; the cited sources are instead listed in the reference task queue.
The adverse-event bowel-frequency atom uses a calculated midpoint (22.5/day) solely to satisfy the current quantitative-result representation while preserving the reported 20-25/day range.
schema_gaps: QuantitativeResult requires a single estimate; reported numeric ranges do not have a dedicated range-only result type, so the diarrhoea-frequency atom explicitly labels its midpoint as calculated and stores the reported range as interval_type=range.
The schema has no dedicated diagnostic-test-result or case-causality-assessment atom kind; diagnostic findings are represented as qualitative_result atoms with outcome context.
